cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Answer the Previous Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every dangerous question by sincerely answering an earlier, safer version of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit down; I'll pour the tea. You asked how lunch was: the soup was excellent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was before I asked who ate my birthday cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll cut you something else while we talk. The soup was a little salty, since you asked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stop offering food. Tell me what happened to the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No food, then. On your earlier question, I wouldn't order the soup again.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls hosting, A3 offers replacement food and A5 withdraws it to keep B talking while answering earlier lunch review.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cake accusation sends A3 back to soup; B4 food refusal causes A5 no-food concession, but A5 never-order conclusion sits awkwardly beside A1 excellent.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants cake accountability and B4 refuses a distractive offer, both credible.

heightening.evidence: A5 adapts service terms and extends safe review, rather than supplying the dangerous identity.

specificity.evidence: A1 tea and lunch; B2 cake; A3 salty soup make the current and prior topics explicit.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 total reversal of soup judgement is unnecessary when less salt would directly develop A3 detail.

coach2.missing: The soup verdict reversal is plausible but not well-earned by slightly salty.
coach2.firstDefect: A5 would-not-order overstates the stated defect.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 rejects A3 distraction and restates the cake demand.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 respects B4 no-food condition while returning to lunch.
